evals.prompt: find a skill for python code review
evals.expected_output: A ranked markdown table of top 10 Claude Code skills / MCP servers for Python code review, with columns: #, Match, Name, Description, Quality, URL. At least 3 sources were searched. Every row has a clickable URL. A one-line explanation of the top result's biggest match and quality driver follows the table.
expectations: Output contains a markdown table with columns # | Match | Name | Description | Quality | URL
At least 3 distinct source URLs are cited (e.g. github.com, smithery.ai, mcp.directory)
Every result row includes a URL — no results without a link
The response includes a one-line explanation after the table about why the top result ranked first
Output does not return npm packages, VS Code extensions, or general software — only skills/MCP/plugins

evals.prompt: is there an MCP server for interacting with Jira tickets?
evals.expected_output: Search results from mcp.directory and Smithery (at minimum) for Jira MCP servers. Returns a ranked table with match and quality scores. If sources fail, notes them as footnotes. Does not invent URLs.
expectations: Output searches at least mcp.directory or Smithery (both are primary MCP registries)
Output contains a ranked table with Match and Quality score columns
Output does not fabricate URLs — every link must resolve to a real-looking domain
If a source returns an error or no results, the skill mentions it as a footnote rather than silently dropping it
Results are scoped to MCP servers or Claude Code skills, not generic Jira integrations or REST clients

evals.prompt: /find-skill 5 generate release notes from git commits
evals.expected_output: Exactly 5 results returned (N=5 parsed correctly from the invocation). Results are for release-notes / changelog generation skills. Ranked table with Match and Quality scores. Sources from at least wshobson/agents, Smithery, or web fallback are checked.
expectations: Response returns exactly 5 rows in the results table (N=5 parsed from invocation prefix)
All results are relevant to release notes, changelog generation, or git commit summarization
A one-line plan is echoed before searching (e.g. 'Searching 6+ marketplaces for release notes skills — returning top 5')
The table includes both Match (0-100) and Quality (0-10) score columns
At least one source from Smithery, wshobson/agents, or mattpocock/skills was attempted
